segments.caption: Nine Test hundreds. No Indian wicketkeeper has more.
MS Dhoni made six, in 90 Tests. Rishabh Pant has nine, in 53.
But the hundreds aren't what make him different.
Line up India's great keepers. Farokh Engineer, two hundreds in 46 Tests. Syed Kirmani, two in 88.
Wriddhiman Saha, three in 40. Dhoni, six in 90.
Pant makes a hundred every six Tests. Dhoni made one every fifteen.
Now the world. Every dot is a leading keeper, placed by average and strike rate.
Most sit here: averaging in the thirties, scoring fifty or sixty runs per hundred balls.
Pant sits up here. Almost 45, at 74. On this chart, only Adam Gilchrist is higher and faster: 47, at 82.
Here's what really sets him apart. Compare each keeper with the top-order batters in his own team.
Watling and Saha scored slower than theirs. Dhoni, six runs per hundred balls faster.
Pant is 25 faster. At Edgbaston, with India 98 for 5, he made 146 off 111 balls.
He doesn't fit into a team's tempo. He changes it.
And he does it with sixes. 108, the most by any wicketkeeper in Test history. Gilchrist hit 100.
At home, he averages almost 50, and against spin he scores at almost a run a ball. Away, he averages almost 43. Dhoni averaged 33 away from home.
Since 2002, India's other keepers have three away hundreds between them. Pant has seven, all in SENA countries, one in each of them. Dhoni never made one there.
Now, the hard part. When he walks in with four down for under 150, Pant averages 34. De Kock and Watling do better.
But watch the fourth innings, when Tests are decided. 114 at the Oval. 97 at Sydney, to save a Test. 89 not out at the Gabba, to win one. 64 at Mumbai, when the rest of the innings added 57.
In fourth innings, he averages 41. Dhoni averaged 33.
And in Tests India lose, Pant still averages 39. Dhoni averaged 27. No keeper here fights harder in defeat.
So, is he India's greatest keeper-batter? By hundreds, by tempo, by what he does away from home, nobody else is close.
The gloves? That's another debate.
Beyond The Scoreboard.
